title: Laomedon
capsule: Laomedon of Mytilene was one of Alexander the Great's companions assigned Syria (including Phoenicia and Palestine) at the Partition of Babylon in 323 BCE following Alexander's death. His hold was brief: in 320 BCE Nicanor, acting for Antipater, ousted him from the satrapy, and the region fell into the contested territory fought over during the First and Second Wars of the Diadochi. Laomedon subsequently disappears from the historical record, his fate unrecorded by surviving sources.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Laomedon's control of Syria is attested only by the Partition of Babylon list in Diodorus Siculus and Justin; his actual territorial administration is unconfirmed by contemporary documentary evidence.
